divergences.old: Reading --owner and --repo context from the first git remote on the connection's host in `git remote -v` order, which is sorted by remote name
divergences.toil: origin is offered first, then the other remotes in that order, and the first on the connection's host wins. The two differ only when origin and a remote whose name sorts before it (mirror, fork) are both on the host
divergences.why: origin is the clone's own remote, so it's the least surprising one to act on when two remotes point at the same server.

divergences.old: github commands putting owner, repo, label and ref into request paths as typed, so a "." or ".." segment (or its %2e or backslash form) is collapsed by URL parsing and the request, a DELETE included, goes to a different resource on the same host
divergences.toil: A path with a "." or ".." segment is refused with INVALID_INPUT before anything is sent: core's requests.path bound for every area, plus a check here that first reads the path as the URL parser does (tab, LF and CR dropped, trailing C0 controls and spaces trimmed), so two dots with a tab between them or a trailing ".. " can't become ".." afterwards.
divergences.why: A write approved for one resource must not land on another: --label ../../../repos/o/r on issue unlabel would otherwise send DELETE /repos/o/r.

divergences.old: github commands putting owner, repo, label and ref into request paths as typed, so a /, ?, # or % in one of them is path or query syntax rather than part of the name (#72 items 4 and 13)
divergences.toil: Every value is encoded as one path segment (core's apiPath), so a label area/api or a ref release/1.4 is sent as area%2Fapi and release%2F1.4. --owner and --repo are refused with INVALID_INPUT if they hold /, \, ?, #, % or a control character, however they arrive: the flag, a toil project, an env var, the connection's setting or the git remote
divergences.why: An id names one resource: a label or ref must reach that label or ref, and an owner or repo can never hold those characters on GitHub.

divergences.old: github pr delete-comment, pr delete-review-comment, issue unlabel, pr remove-reviewers and issue unassign available to every caller
divergences.toil: The same commands on the CLI; toil mcp never serves them
divergences.why: Deletes are never exposed through MCP (CLAUDE.md, Writes).

divergences.old: github pr list, pr comments, pr review-comments, pr files, pr reviews and commit checks paging until a short page, with no limit on the number of pages
divergences.toil: The same short-page stop, plus a bound: after 1,000 pages (100,000 items) the command fails with HTTP, naming what was being paged, and fix text to narrow the request
divergences.why: A server that ignores the page parameter would otherwise be asked for the same page forever; the bound turns a hang into an error that says what happened.

divergences.old: github pr threads printing "warning: more than N review threads ..." to stderr when the first 100 threads aren't all of them
divergences.toil: The same text as a GITHUB_REVIEW_THREADS_TRUNCATED entry in meta.warnings; data is unchanged
divergences.why: An MCP client never sees stderr, so a truncation it can't see would fail silently. meta.warnings is the envelope's place for it (Output Contract).

divergences.old: GraphQL failures (review threads, pr status, auto-merge, merge queue, drafts, pr resolve) reported as the joined error messages alone, or "GraphQL response contained no data"
divergences.toil: "GitHub GraphQL error: <messages joined with '; '>", or "GitHub answered the GraphQL query at <url> with no data.", both as HTTP with a fix, from core's one GraphQL helper
divergences.why: Every area's GraphQL calls fail the same way, saying which service failed and what to check next.

divergences.old: github issue label typing its data as { labels: [...] }
divergences.toil: data is GitHub's answer passed through unchanged, as the contract specifies. GitHub answers with a bare array of labels, so the typed field the contract records never exists at run time
divergences.why: Nothing changes; the recorded field comes from a declared type, not from what GitHub returns, and a fixture shaped like the real API can't carry it.

divergences.old: github pr add-reviewers typing its data as { url, users, teams }
divergences.toil: data is GitHub's answer passed through unchanged, as the contract specifies. GitHub answers a reviewer request with the pull request, which has url and requested_reviewers but no users or teams
divergences.why: Nothing changes; the recorded fields come from a declared type, not from what GitHub returns, and a fixture shaped like the real API can't carry them.
